+title: 'Decide the web clocks under runCode: fetch timeout argument, search per-provider timeout, URLRequest timeoutInterval'
+---
+## What
+**Blocked on a decision of the user. An agent must not select the option.**
+
+The web verbs run as inner `tools.web.*` calls inside a `runCode` snippet. The outer, tool-level clock is the `runCode` timeout. Three web clocks are under it:
+
+1. **Fetch timeout.** `tools.web.fetch` takes a `timeout` argument in the range 1…120 s. The default is 30 s (`WebFetchPolicy.defaultFetchTimeout`, `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/Web/WebConfiguration.swift`; range in `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/Web/Fetch.swift`; enforced in `WebFetcher.swift` `load(_:timeout:guarded:)`). It gives `WebFetchFailure.timeout`, and the snippet can catch it and continue. A 120 s fetch can never report its own timeout, because the `runCode` limit is also 120 s. The `@Guide` text "Omit it for 30" in `Fetch.swift` is a second copy of the default and can drift.
+2. **Search timeout for each provider.** `searchTimeout` is 10 s (`WebConfiguration.swift`, used in `WebSearchChain.swift` near line 101). When it fires, the chain goes to the next provider. This is a fail-over rule, not only a safety bound.
+3. **`URLRequest.timeoutInterval`** (`WebFetcher.swift` `prepare(_:timeout:)`) is set to at least the limit. URLSession always has some request timeout (default 60 s), so it cannot be removed. The doc calls it a backstop.
+
+Options for the user:
+- **A. Keep 2 and 3, remove the model argument of 1.** A fetch has no own clock. Only the `runCode` clock bounds it. Keep the search fail-over, because it selects a provider and does not bound the tool.
+- **B. Keep all three as functional per-request limits** (a failed fetch is a value that the snippet uses). Only cap the fetch `timeout` range below `executionTimeLimit` and make the `@Guide` text read the constant.
+- **C. Remove all own web clocks.** Set `timeoutInterval` to a large value, and let only the `runCode` clock bound the web calls. The search chain then cannot skip a slow provider.
+
+After the decision, the subtasks are:
+- [ ] Change `Fetch.swift`, `WebConfiguration.swift`, `WebFetcher.swift`, `WebSearchChain.swift` per the decision.
+- [ ] Update the web unit tests (`Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/WebVerbArgumentTests.swift` `fetchSchemaBoundsTimeout`, and the fetch/search timeout tests).
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] No web clock can have the same value as, or a larger value than, the `runCode` tool timeout.
+- [ ] The default fetch timeout has one source. The `@Guide` text does not contain a second literal.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Update `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/WebVerbArgumentTests.swift` for the new argument range or schema.
+- [ ] `swift test --filter Web` passes. `swift test` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #timeouts #web #stuck
\ No newline at end of file
